conviction_note: Two modest positives (a stale peer read-through and the easiest LIFO comp of the year) sum to +1.9, and I cut the emitted number to +1.2 because three things all push the other way: this shareholder base has sold six of the last seven prints including Q3 FY26 where EPS +7.7% and domestic SSS +4.1% bought -8.99%, so the reaction function has demonstrated it does not pay for a comp beat; my sign agrees with the sealed skew (-2.81 vol points, calls bid, 'upside paid'), so most of any bounce thesis is already in the option price; and the honest counterweights are real and unpriced-in-my-favour (gasoline averaged ~$4.06-4.19/gal in August 2026 and is higher YoY in every state, same-SKU inflation is collapsing from 'just north of 7%' toward ORLY's guided 1-2% which pressures AZO's guided mid-4% ticket, and the +3.7% domestic SSS bar laps a +4.8% base). On the most heavily covered name in the window a near-zero is the honest answer and +1.2 is close to it.
bar: Revenue $6.71bn for Q4 FY26 (16 weeks ended 2026-08-29), +7.5% on $6.24bn, and domestic same-store sales +3.7% - agreed by two sources: https://news.alphastreet.com/autozone-azo-q4-2026-preview-eps-est-54-22-reports-september-22/ (21 analysts, $54.22 EPS, $6.71bn) and https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/autozone-stock-faces-earnings-watch-before-september-22/70142898 ($54.30 EPS, $6.71bn). The EPS bar is NOT tight - $54.22 / $54.30 / $54.78 (sweep calendar row) across three sources, range $51.46-$56.97 - so I size against the revenue/comp bar and cap every finding small on the EPS line.
positioning_check: Short interest 434,741 shares = 2.67% of a 16.27m float, 2.66% of shares outstanding, short ratio 1.94 days to cover, up marginally from 432,888 the prior month. Verified myself at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/azo/statistics/ read 2026-09-21. That is not a crowded short: there is no squeeze mechanism to amplify a positive and no forced-covering fuel, which is a reason my positive sizes stay small. The sealed baseline's 25-delta skew is -2.81 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid') with put/call OI 0.95 - so the option market is already leaning the way I am leaning, after a 34% de-rate to a 52-week low. On the implied-move check the sweep asked for: the 2026-10-16 front expiry is 25 days out and does NOT span an FOMC, ATM IV is 47.5% against 22.8% realised 20d vol, and the 8.36% event move is consistent with this name's LAST THREE reactions (-8.99%, -6.32%, -7.17%) rather than its 7-event median of 3.42% - so the anchor looks like a genuine event premium, not macro contamination, and I treat ~7-8% as the honest width of the outcome distribution.

findings.finding: The two peer prints that re-rated AZO both stopped measuring before AZO's quarter did: Advance Auto Parts' Q2 (12 weeks, quarter beginning after its Q1 ended 2026-04-25, so ending mid-July) reported comp -0.5% on 2026-08-20 and took AZO down 4% that day, but AZO's Q4 runs to 2026-08-29 and the only direct peer datapoint that covers July says demand stepped UP - O'Reilly on 2026-08-07: 'we did not realize the normal ramp up in demand for certain hot-weather-related categories' in June, then 'We have definitely seen summer take hold across our markets in July' with a 'step-up in sales results to start the third quarter,' particularly hot-weather categories - and NOAA has since recorded summer 2026 as the warmest in the 132-year US record (+3.0F) with August 2026 the warmest August on record, against AZO management's stated Q4 planning assumption of 'normal summer weather'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the domestic same-store-sales line and this name has NOT paid for it. Q3 FY26 (2026-05-26) printed domestic SSS +4.1% with EPS +7.7% and the stock fell 8.99%; the two prints before that fell 6.32% and 7.17%. Six of the seven reactions in the sealed baseline are negative. A comp beat alone has bought nothing here for three quarters, which is why this is sized at a fraction of its fundamental content.
findings.why_not_priced: The price shows the market took the opposite read and took it on a stale window: AZO fell 4% to $2,961 on 2026-08-20 explicitly on AAP's DIY miss (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/20/advance-auto-parts-plunges-21-as-revenue-miss-overshadows-earnings-beat-autozone-falls-4-oreilly-automotive-slips/) and has since made a new 52-week low with TD Cowen, Oppenheimer and Citi all cutting targets into the print. If the market had weighted ORLY's July step-up and the record-hot August that sit inside AZO's quarter and outside AAP's, AZO would not be marking to AAP's mid-July four weeks, the sell-side targets would not be falling in the week the NOAA record was published, and the run-up would not be -4.75% over five sessions.
findings.independence: Two different sources point the same way from different directions: NOAA/NCEI's August and summer 2026 temperature record (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/news/national-climate-202608) is the macro series, and ORLY's own management commentary is the direct-counterparty statement of the transmission mechanism. They share no document. The honest limit, and it is the reason this is 1.3 and not 3: the July leg is stated by a counterparty, the August leg is my inference from a weather series, and reasoning from weather is explicitly on the list of what has NOT paid in this stage's resolved days.

findings.finding: AZO's LIFO reserve has been built entirely by tariff inflation - the 10-Q states 'Due to price changes on the Company's merchandise purchases, primarily due to inflation driven by tariffs, the Company's LIFO credit reserve balance was $260.0 million at May 9, 2026, and $83.0 million at August 30, 2025' - and Q4 FY26 carries the easiest LIFO comp of the year (guided ~$30m charge, 45bp, against an actual $80m charge / 128bp in Q4 FY25), with upside to a credit if supplier pass-back of IEEPA refunds lowers replacement cost in the May-August window, which is the exact line the stock has been sold on for three consecutive quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin with LIFO as the swing factor is the stated cause of the last three selloffs: Q3 FY26 gross margin 52.2%, -57bp, with a 77bp LIFO charge cited as the primary driver, and the stock fell 8.99%; Q4 FY25 gross margin 51.5%, -98bp on a 128bp LIFO impact, and EPS fell 5.6% reported against +8.7% ex-LIFO. The market has punished this line hard when it went the wrong way; it has never been tested with it going the right way on this name, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate is small.
findings.why_not_priced: Only the delta to the guide is unpriced and I say so: the $30m Q4 charge was guided on the 2026-05-26 call, so the +83bp YoY improvement is inside what the company already told the market to expect and is a reported-quarter item. What is not in any preview I could find is that the reserve is now $260m built from tariff inflation that the Supreme Court voided on 2026-02-20, and that peer retailers are already booking the reversal - AAP took $26m of tariff refunds worth 130bp of gross margin in its July quarter, Target applied $685m of $730m of refunds to reduce COGS, and ORLY says it is negotiating supplier sharing of refunds. If the market had priced a possible LIFO credit rather than the guided charge, the sell-side gross-margin cuts into this print would not be running the other way.
findings.independence: Independent of finding 1 - different document (the 10-Q, not a peer transcript) and a different P&L line (gross margin, not comp). Corroboration from a different source: https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/oreilly-automotive-suppliers-sharing-tariff-refund-benefits/827111/ on supplier pass-back, and AAP's own $26m / 130bp refund benefit in the quarter ending mid-July. The counterweight I have already netted into the 0.6: the upside-to-guide leg rests on other retailers' cost behaviour, not on an AZO document, and AZO itself reports and is modelled on ex-LIFO EPS, so the market has a habit of looking through this line in both directions.

outside_window.finding: The FY2026 10-K, due roughly late October 2026, is where the full-year LIFO reserve roll-forward and any IEEPA tariff refund or gain-contingency disclosure will appear in primary form; CBP's CAPE liquidation process was still running at ~$128.7bn of accepted refunds as of 2026-07-31, so supplier pass-back to AZO continues to accrue after this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: A direct IEEPA tariff refund receivable or gain contingency in AZO's own filings - the Q3 FY26 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/866787/000110465926073525/azo-20260509x10q.htm) carries no IEEPA, refund, customs or gain-contingency language at all, and AZO's model is supplier-as-importer-of-record like ORLY's, so there is no AAP-style direct refund line to find here

FX as an edge: I computed it and it is not differentiated. FRED DEXMXUS monthly averages (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DEXMXUS) give USD/MXN ~17.30 across May-Aug 2026 against ~18.97 across May-Aug 2025, a ~9.7% YoY peso tailwind - but that is SMALLER than the ~15% YoY move in the Q3 window that produced the $74m sales / $0.83 EPS benefit, so naively scaling Q3's FX benefit over 16 weeks overstates Q4 by roughly $0.40. Decelerating tailwind, routinely modelled, no edge

A buyback slowdown: none detectable. $586.3m / 164k shares at $3,582 in Q3, $800m remaining, then a further $1.5bn authorised 2026-06-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000117184326004150/exh_991.htm) and $850m of 4.950% notes due 2031 completed 2026-07-14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000110465926083528/tm2620403d1_8k.htm). The financing question answered: the money terms out commercial paper and funds repurchase capacity, corroborated by the incremental authorisation - it is not distress and it is not a finding
A quiet 8-K, management change or unusual filing in the run-in - AZO's only 8-Ks since June 2026 are the buyback authorisation and the two notes-offering filings
A squeeze setup - 2.67% of float short and 1.94 days to cover leaves no mechanism in either direction

Gasoline prices as a positive - they are a negative and they cut against me: US averages of roughly $4.05 (June), $3.93 (July) and $4.06-4.19 (August) 2026, higher YoY in every state (https://www.lendingtree.com/credit-cards/study/us-gas-prices/), which supports AAP's 'tighter household budgets' DIY read rather than mine, and I have netted it into the sizes rather than filing it twice
baseline_tension: My findings AGREE with the sealed skew (-2.81 vol points, calls bid, 'upside paid') and therefore are probably substantially in the price already, which is the main reason the emitted number is well below the sum of the findings; they cut AGAINST the run-up (-4.5% over 20d, -4.75% over 5d, a 52-week low on the day before the print), and that run-up is precisely what I claim is a stale peer read-through from a quarter that ended six weeks before AZO's.
lessons_applied: 'What has worked' names weather reasoning explicitly as what has NOT paid - my largest finding was a weather finding, so I cut it 2.0 -> 1.3, rebuilt its spine on the part of the same paragraph that IS on the worked list ('a peer's print landing after the company last spoke, leaving consensus stale' - ORLY 2026-08-07 and AAP 2026-08-20, both after AZO last spoke on 2026-05-26), and said in independence which leg is counterparty-stated and which leg is my inference from a temperature series

Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series; macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until a counterparty says it): kept the finding because ORLY, a direct counterparty, stated the July transmission in its own words, but held the size down because the August leg has no counterparty statement behind it

Rule 6 (verify the bar; a finding inside the guide is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): found three disagreeing EPS consensus figures ($54.22 / $54.30 / $54.78), so I sized against the revenue/comp bar that two sources agree on ($6.71bn, +3.7% domestic SSS), said the EPS bar is loose, and cut the LIFO finding 1.2 -> 0.6 because the $30m Q4 charge was company-guided on 2026-05-26 and only the delta to that guide is unpriced

Rule 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): my sign agrees with a calls-bid skew, so I discounted rather than treating the skew as colour, and I confirmed there is no crowded short to amplify a positive (2.67% of float, 1.94 days)

Rule 1 and rule 3 (the reaction function has veto power; the caveat must reach the number): widened the gap between the finding sum and the emitted move from 3.2/2.0 to 1.9/1.2, and the conviction note now states the size of the cut and the three reasons for it explicitly

Rule 2 (name the line): checked whether the LIFO item is a one_off - it is not, it sits in gross margin inside the reported quarter - but noted in the finding that AZO reports and is modelled on ex-LIFO EPS, which is the same look-through risk rule 2 warns about, and sized accordingly

Rule 8 (understatement is the systematic error) was considered and deliberately NOT applied: it is scoped to thin coverage and a confirmed company-level number, and this is a 21-estimate, $46.6bn name where neither finding is an AZO primary-document number

Rule 3 (read the set): checked that my two findings do not rest on one document and cannot both be false for the same reason - they are a peer transcript on the comp line and a 10-Q on the gross-margin line - and moved the gasoline-price and SKU-deflation counterweights into the conviction note and searched_and_found_nothing rather than filing a contradictory negative finding beside two positives
